correctness.rationale: For each single exchange, a teaching sample must hit the two coordinates that change. Conversely if a different tree T′ agrees on the sample, take e∈T minus T′ and an f∈T′ crossing the cut of T−e. Such an f is outside T; both changing edges are unqueried, and they form an exchange. Thus the vertex-cover criterion is exact for every sample. König gives the cardinality result. For weights place query costs on source-to-tree and cotree-to-sink arcs and use a capacity above the sum of all costs on each directed tree-to-cotree exchange arc; finite optimal cuts give precisely minimum-cost covers. Hall on F⊂T counts |F| tree and |N(F)| cotree edges crossing the components of T−F. Tree packing gives the Hall inequalities; for the converse, refine any partition into its induced connected components without changing the crossing count and choose T connected within each refined part, so the corresponding F gives the required partition bound. On the other side, taking F=N(Y) for cotree edges Y implies F∪Y has the same components as forest F, so under the two-forest bound |Y|≤|F|. Conversely a violating induced connected subgraph admits an internal tree extended to T, and its internal cotree edges violate Hall. The K_{p,q} cases are exhaustive: a singleton shore is a tree; two stars cover a two-vertex shore; the listed K_{3,3} remaining four edges form a path; the two disjoint K_{3,4} trees extend by two separately assigned edges at each new vertex. At K_{3,4}, r=c and both characterizations apply. The bridged K5 example has an isolated bridge coordinate in the exchange graph and a core with two disjoint spanning trees, so it gives 4 versus bounds 5 and 6. An independent replay, python3 /workspace/checks/05_cover_certificate.py, exhaustively compared every sample with all-tree and single-exchange consistency for 3,494 target/sample pairs over 43 connected graphs through four vertices (135 targets), and checked the K_{3,4} packing. Larger frozen verification counts are recorded evidence, not a fresh run.

value.rationale: Testing sample uniqueness against all spanning trees could involve exponentially many hypotheses. The exact criterion reduces all those constraints to one bipartite instance determined by fundamental paths, and supports minimum-cost teaching even when positive and negative edges have different costs. The graph-wide extremal statements characterize when one of the two obvious samples is optimal for all targets, and give an exact uniform value for a canonical graph family. The value is the teaching application and local-to-global bridge, not a new proof of bipartite matching duality or matroid union.
